title: Select Investments Within Capital
real_world_story: An investor has a fixed amount of capital and several investment opportunities. Each investment requires a certain amount of capital and provides an expected value. An investment can either be completely selected or rejected.

real_world_connection.input_represents: Investment costs and expected portfolio values
real_world_connection.target_represents: Maximum portfolio value achievable within the available capital
real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Selecting or rejecting each investment while respecting the capital limit

problem_statement: Given N investment opportunities, each with a required capital and expected value, and a maximum available capital, determine the maximum total expected value that can be obtained. Each investment can be selected at most once.
task: Select a subset of investments that maximizes the total expected value without exceeding the available capital.
input_format: The first line contains two integers N and C, representing the number of investments and the maximum available capital. The next N lines contain two integers capital and value for each investment.
output_format: Print the maximum total expected value achievable within the available capital.

examples.explanation: Selecting investments requiring 5 and 2 units of capital gives a total value of 10 while using exactly 7 units of capital.
The investment requiring 4 units of capital provides the maximum achievable value of 7.

expected_algorithm.name: 0/1 Knapsack
expected_algorithm.reason: Each investment can either be selected once or rejected, making this a 0/1 Knapsack optimization problem.

hint: Create a DP array representing the maximum value for every capital limit.
For each investment, decide whether to select it or skip it.
Process capital limits in decreasing order so that each investment is selected at most once.
The value at the maximum capital gives the optimal portfolio value.
real_world_takeaway: 0/1 Knapsack helps investors choose a combination of indivisible investment opportunities when available capital is limited.
